# EXP-WPC-004 - SC-6 CHANGED-pair forensics (label-free, descriptive; generated by `scripts/wpc_sc6_forensics.py`)

Scope: frozen scores + cached traces only; **nothing was scored or evaluated** (no AUROC); V10 / V9c-val used descriptively only. 'Invisible' := frozen `sbg_v5 == 0` (exact). 'Partner' := label-0 primary row with the same `group` (same SP transform, no SC-6; cross-checked against the repo's `matched_pair_id`/`matched_equivalent_pair_id`: 0 mismatches).

## 2. SC-6 edit (all pairs)

- v10_test: 23/23 pairs - every changed line (partner->variant, parentheses ignored) is a `return` line. Observed forms: `return X` -> `return not X`; `return <const>` -> `return <const> + 1`.
- v9c_val: 18/18 pairs - every changed line (partner->variant, parentheses ignored) is a `return` line. Observed forms: `return X` -> `return not X`; `return <const>` -> `return <const> + 1`.
- v9c_dev: 18/18 pairs - every changed line (partner->variant, parentheses ignored) is a `return` line. Observed forms: `return X` -> `return not X`; `return <const>` -> `return <const> + 1`.
- v9c_train: 62/62 pairs - every changed line (partner->variant, parentheses ignored) is a `return` line. Observed forms: `return X` -> `return not X`; `return <const>` -> `return <const> + 1`.

Full unified diffs (partner->variant isolates SC-6; base->variant also shown): `sc6_diffs_<split>.txt`; one-line auto descriptions in the CSV column `sc6_edit_desc_auto` (rule-based; for V10 verified by reading all 23 diffs: every SC-6 edit is a final-`return` expression mutation, e.g. `return result` -> `return not result`).

## 3. Trace channels and cause classes for v5==0 pairs

Channel comparison uses **PV = partner-vs-variant** (SP transform cancels, same SP seed) as primary basis; BV (base-vs-variant) columns are in the CSV but are confounded by the SP edit (line-event skeleton/coverage differ on SP-transformed code). Run 0 only is stored in the cache. Locals snapshots compared at c/r/e events only, after masking `0x...` addresses.

| split | zero pairs | A | B | C | D | D: truncated (lean if ignored) | D: cache missing | zero pairs with PV skeleton identical | PV c/r/e snapshots identical | PV ret differs on >=1 input |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v10_test | 17 | 16 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 ({'A': 1}) | 0 | 17 | 17 | 17 |
| v9c_val | 10 | 8 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 ({'A': 1}) | 0 | 10 | 10 | 9 |
| v9c_dev | 8 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 ({}) | 0 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| v9c_train | 31 | 21 | 0 | 7 | 3 | 2 ({'A': 2}) | 1 | 30 | 30 | 23 |

Definitions (decided on PV): **A** ret differs on >=1 input, exc/stdout identical, full event skeleton (type+function incl. line events) identical, every c/r/e locals snapshot identical; **B** as A but a c/r/e snapshot differs (and abstract-domain snapshots identical - see below); **C** ret/exc/stdout identical on all 11 inputs; **D** other (truncated traces, missing cache, exc/stdout/skeleton differ, or abstract snapshot differs). **B = 0 everywhere**: before masking memory addresses many pairs looked like B because snapshots hold `<function ... at 0x...>` reprs that differ between processes; after masking, no zero-score pair has any other differing recorded local.

Honest limits: (i) the cache keeps locals snapshots only at c/r/e events; line-event snapshots (which the frozen state genome consumes) are NOT in the cache, so class A means 'no difference in recorded c/r/e locals', not 'no difference in any local at any line' (for a pure `return <expr>` edit there is no new local by construction, which is consistent with A); (ii) only run 0 of 5 runs is stored; (iii) `ret` reprs are capped at 1500 chars; (iv) class C = battery-blind on 11 inputs only - the label oracle's differing input is not recoverable here (UNKNOWN); (v) the 'abstract domain collapse' (class B) was not observed, so it is not supported as a cause by this evidence.

### Task 4 - does the returned value appear in the `r`-event locals of the entry function? (zero-score pairs, variant)

| split | pairs with ret present among r-snapshot values on >=1 input (all inputs) | same, non-trivial values only | on inputs where ret differs from partner: pairs with ret in locals (>=1 input) | (all differing inputs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v10_test | 10 | 4 | 1 | 0 |
| v9c_val | 3 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| v9c_dev | 4 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| v9c_train | 14 | 1 | 4 | 1 |

(Exact string match of `repr(ret)` to a snapshot value of the entry function's last `r` event; snapshot values capped at 100 chars, long returns compared on the first 90 chars; 'non-trivial' excludes None/True/False/0/1/-1/empty containers. Matches on inputs where ret is unchanged are coincidental, hence the restriction to differing inputs. The mutated return value (`not X`, `X + 1`) is by construction not a local, so the changed value is not recorded in the snapshot.)

## 5. Anomalies / data problems

- v10_test: zero-score pairs whose raw PV c/r/e snapshots differ ONLY by memory address reprs: 10 (all pairs: 13).
- v9c_val: zero-score pairs whose raw PV c/r/e snapshots differ ONLY by memory address reprs: 6 (all pairs: 9).
- v9c_dev: zero-score pairs whose raw PV c/r/e snapshots differ ONLY by memory address reprs: 3 (all pairs: 10).
- v9c_train: zero-score pairs whose raw PV c/r/e snapshots differ ONLY by memory address reprs: 8 (all pairs: 14).
- Cached snapshots contain process-specific `<function ... at 0x...>` reprs (nondeterministic across extractions); the frozen abstract domain maps them to NON_NULL so scores are unaffected, but raw snapshot equality is unusable without masking.
- v9c SP-8 'equivalent' partners can be broken: visible SC-6+SP-8 pairs whose SP-only partner has exception_fraction>0 -> val 3, dev 3, train 7 (e.g. val `math_largest_rect_hist__sp-8_s2`: `UnboundLocalError` on all inputs, exception_fraction 1.0). Their large v5 (0.28-0.68) is then driven by exceptions of the SP transform itself. Not investigated further (outside scope).
- v9c_train: `math_gray_code` is absent from the trace cache -> its 2 SC-6 pairs (1 zero-score, 1 visible) have no trace evidence (UNKNOWN; counted D).
- Truncated traces (event cap) in a few pairs prevent a clean classification -> D, with the lean if truncation were ignored shown above.
- In v9c splits the partner comes from the v8 SP pipeline while the SC-6 variant comes from v9_composed, so partner->variant diffs contain cosmetic parenthesisation differences (ignored in descriptions/flags).
- Base->variant comparisons: the SP transform alone changes the line-event skeleton/coverage, so BV classification is not meaningful (almost all D); see `cause_class_if_BV`.
- Anomaly list from consistency checks (partner count != 1, matched-id mismatch, v5==0 but v3!=0): none.

## 6. Reproduction

```
cd IEEE_ACCESS_PRE_SUBMISSION/WP_C_ABLATIONS/scripts
export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
../../../venvs/py313/bin/python wpc_sc6_forensics.py          # ~0.5 s; refuses to overwrite existing outputs
```

Outputs: `sc6_pairs_<split>.csv` (one row per pair, all channel fields), `sc6_diffs_<split>.txt`, `sc6_summary.json`, this file.
